name: Advanced Filter Workspace
purpose: Make a collection query explicit, reversible and understandable while distinguishing edited filters from the results currently displayed.
useWhen: A collection has several meaningful criteria or operators repeatedly refine a result scope.
avoidWhen: There is no queryable collection or only one fixed record.
A simple short list can be scanned without filter state or an advanced panel.

states.meaning: Active query matches current controls or committed draft.
states.presentation: Show active chips, scope and exact or qualified result count.

states.meaning: Controls differ from the displayed active query.
states.presentation: Mark unapplied changes without showing a draft count as current results.
Keep active query visible and qualify retained stale count.
Retain active conditions and offer clear or remove a criterion.
Keep draft and active values distinct and show retry.

transitions.focus: Keep clear trigger; active query becomes declared defaults.
Keep apply control; commit draft and reset page.
Keep reset button; restore draft from active query.
Keep filter focus; politely announce new count.
Retain filter control; announce persistent retry.
Retain clear control or nearest summary heading after removal.

visual.hierarchy: Scope and text search lead; frequent facets precede advanced criteria; active conditions remain visible beside result count.
visual.alignment: Align search and facet labels to a shared grid and align active summary with the result collection.
visual.spacing: Keep label-control spacing smaller than the gap between facet groups; separate reset from the primary apply action.
visual.typography: Use a clear section label and normal control labels; render active values with enough weight to distinguish them from hints.
visual.emphasis: Highlight Apply only for unapplied draft changes; active count is supporting information, not a competing headline.
visual.surfaces: Use a single coherent filter region; chips mark conditions rather than decorative tags around all metadata.
visual.proportions: Size controls for plausible long option names; let multi-select summaries wrap before truncating selected meaning.
visual.discoverability: Show active filter count when collapsed and keep Clear all available without reopening every facet.
visual.states: Distinguish stale results, pending requests, draft changes and zero matches using explicit labels.
visual.brand: Reuse the product control, spacing and selected-state tokens; preserve focus and status contrast when adapting brand.

keyboard.when: Filter controls and active condition removals.
keyboard.result: Follow visible label and group order; removal buttons name the condition.
keyboard.focus: On removal, use next chip or active-summary heading.

keyboard.result: Submit the draft query without submitting an unrelated edit form.
keyboard.focus: Keep search focus and announce results.

keyboard.result: Close the panel with its declared draft policy.
keyboard.focus: Return to the filter trigger; a nonmodal panel must not trap focus.

accessibility.naming: Give the region a task-specific heading and each control a persistent name.
accessibility.semantics: Use a named search region, fieldsets for facets and a polite result status. Announce committed query changes rather than every keystroke. Native controls keep their keyboard model; modal mobile presentation requires a labeled dialog with focus containment and return.

checks.requirement: Every task and recovery action can be completed with keyboard input.
checks.passEvidence: Record the starting focus, complete the task and verify a visible logical destination.

responsive.condition: Inline facets crowd search or leave too little room for results.
responsive.restructure: Move advanced facets to a labeled panel or modal sheet while leaving active count, query summary and reset accessible.
responsive.focusContinuity: Return to the same filter trigger on close; result replacement does not steal input focus.

density.useWhen: Mixed input methods, occasional use or unfamiliar terminology.
constraints: Keep controls independently reachable without overlapping hit areas.
Allow user text sizing and wrapping to determine minimum row or field height.

density.useWhen: Repeated scanning by experienced operators with a measured information need.
constraints: Reduce surrounding padding before reducing readable text size.
Preserve focus outline clearance, labels and distinct control targets.

motion.purpose: Explain a local state change without interrupting the current task.
motion.trigger: User initiated disclosure or result replacement.
motion.reduced: Replace content immediately; keep textual progress and completion feedback.
motion.interruption: Cancel obsolete transitions; never queue animation behind new input or block retry.

recovery.explanation: Retry the active query without discarding draft.
Offer the default query or removal of one condition.

checks.requirement: Long labels, absent values and permission restrictions remain distinguishable.
checks.passEvidence: Inspect narrow and wide views with synthetic long labels and missing data.

checks.requirement: Failure preserves user intent and exposes an operable next step.
checks.passEvidence: Inject failure, retry and confirm identity, entered values and focus remain coherent.

checks.requirement: Only shareable, nonsensitive active query values enter URL state when deep linking is appropriate.
checks.passEvidence: Reload/back restores the same active scope; drafts and sensitive free text are excluded by declared policy.

anatomy.purpose: Search record text without confusing it with selected facets.
Group independent criteria with named values.
Expose active conditions and reversible removal.
Report current result count and query progress.
Apply draft or clear/reset defined scopes.

variants.useWhen: Queries are cheap and incremental changes are predictable.
guidance: Apply facet changes immediately; debounce text search without delaying keyboard editing.
Cancel or ignore stale responses using query identity; count always belongs to the displayed active query.
Treat change then apply as one atomic user operation in the shared state model; never display an intermediate unapplied draft in immediate mode.

variants.useWhen: Queries are costly, interdependent or require deliberate review.
guidance: Keep draft controls distinct from active conditions and show unapplied changes.
Apply commits draft atomically and resets page to the first result; closing the panel retains or discards draft according to an explicit policy.
Reset draft restores the active query without changing results; a separately labeled Clear and apply action explicitly commits the default query.

requires: URL serialization policy excluding sensitive values
composition.focusOwner: Filter control owns editing focus; workspace owns result replacement and mobile overlay lifecycle.
